Department Overview


Safety Process and Risk Research Process Analysts (SPRR PAs) are a global team within the Risk Assessment and Management (RAM) organisation of Pfizer Worldwide Medical and Safety (WMS). We work to provide a variety of safety functions for all Pfizer products on the market and in clinical programs. Pharmacovigilance activities help to monitor the safety profile of all products from clinical development through to post-marketed stages. These activities ensure compliance with regulatory agencies and health authorities in all markets where we hold licences, and ultimately ensure our medicines remain safe and beneficial to patients.


What can I achieve and what will I be responsible for whilst completing a placement at Pfizer?


Pfizer provides you with the opportunity to work with experts in the pharmaceutical industry and has a wealth of opportunities available across a variety of departments. Within Pfizer’s Worldwide Safety department, you can look forward to working with colleagues across different safety-related functions; developing an understanding of pharmacovigilance; experiencing how the monitoring of serious adverse drug reactions influences the benefit risk profile of Pfizer products across various therapeutic areas; as well as building critical business skills and being a valued team member.

Working as an Undergraduate Pharmacovigilance Process Analyst, you will work on product-related and non-product projects to support SPRR activities and safety processes, compliance activities and performance metrics.

Your roles and opportunities may include a selection of the following:

  • Attending Risk Management Committee meetings, supporting Process Analysts (PAs) with meeting outcomes and related activities, which may include: documentation of minutes, tracking actions, signal management tasks.
  • Working with Process Analysts (PAs) and Safety Risk Leads (SRLs) to manage/maintain various Pfizer safety systems, including tools used for: tracking and evaluation of safety signals; monitoring of targeted medical events; monitoring ongoing safety data/topics; visualising and presenting safety data from ongoing clinical trials.
  • Independently seeking out resources and training modules on topics related to safety processes and Pfizer digital tools, training/advising team members, and working to incorporate learnings into team activities.
  • Leading and participating in ad-hoc projects to support and provide continuous improvement initiatives within the team.
  • Supporting a range of safety processes, which may include meeting facilitation, preparing and visualising data, updating and communicating safety information/documentation.
  • Supporting the safety monitoring activities of marketed products and those under clinical development.
  • Collaborating with global colleagues and building professional relationships using Pfizer’s digital tools.

Skills you will develop may include the following:

  • Communication skills through liaising with colleagues.
  • Presentation skills when presenting work at meetings.
  • Organisational/prioritisation skills when working on a variety of projects/tasks.
  • Teamwork through collaboration and networking with various groups and individuals.
  • Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office 365 applications and other safety systems.

What other opportunities and benefits do Pfizer offer?


Pfizer offers a dynamic early careers community, giving you the opportunity to build your professional network with other undergraduates and apprentices. Pfizer offers a variety of volunteering opportunities in our local and STEM communities. Pfizer also offers access to a variety of internal colleague communities and external industry associations, depending on your interests. There may be opportunities to attend pharmacovigilance related training sessions or cross-industry conferences, depending on availability.

Placements will start on 1st September 2027 and will run for 12 months.

title: Senior Officer, Advocacy, International Relations and Policy Planning, North America Team (16 month LTE)
description:
The Foundation

We are the largest nonprofit fighting poverty, disease, and inequity around the world. Founded on a simple premise: people everywhere, regardless of identity or circumstances, should have the chance to live healthy, productive lives. We believe our employees should reflect the rich diversity of the global populations we aim to serve. We provide an exceptional benefits package to employees and their families which include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with no premiums, generous paid time off, paid family leave, foundation-paid retirement contribution, regional holidays, and opportunities to engage in several employee communities. As a workplace, we’re committed to creating an environment for you to thrive both personally and professionally.

The Team

The mission of the Global Policy & Advocacy (GPA) division is to understand and shape the public policy debates affecting the foundation's work, build support for its major program and policy objectives, and develop partnerships and alliances that can advance the foundation's objectives nationally and globally. Because the foundation's resources alone are not enough to solve the challenges ahead, GPA also supports advocacy efforts to engage diverse stakeholders and promote innovative solutions that advance our program goals. We work in close partnership with grantees, our colleagues in the Global Health, Global Development, Global Growth & Opportunity, U.S. and Gender Equality programs and Communications to build the environment in which all people can lead healthy and productive lives.

The North America Team (NAT) is a team within GPA that develops and executes policy, advocacy, communications and government relations strategies to build political support and advance domestic and global programmatic priorities that are funded by, or executed within, the United States, Canada, and the United Nations.

Your Role
The Senior Officer, Advocacy, International Relations and Policy Planning (IRPP), North America Team, will be responsible for translating foundation strategies and priorities into policy-relevant arguments and advocacy opportunities across priority IRPP markets, including Canada and the UN. The role will also lead special advocacy initiatives to advance maternal and child survival through sport and new partnerships, and related to global AI governance.

Working closely with the Deputy Director, Canada and UN leads, AI policy lead, and partnering with program, policy, communications, and other teams across the foundation, this role will support a collaborative, One Foundation approach to market engagement. The successful candidate will bring strong political and institutional judgment, the ability to synthesize complex global health and development strategies, and experience connecting programmatic priorities to the political economy and institutional context of government and multilateral audiences.


*This is a 16 month limited term employment role. Salary plus benefits are provided. Relocation assistance and employer Visa support are not available for this role. Role can be located in Seattle, WA or Washington, DC.


*Applications accepted until 5 PM Pacific Time on Wednesday, November 18, 2026.

*Must have unrestricted work authorization in the country where this position is located. The Foundation does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. This includes direct company sponsorship and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (eg: H-1B, O-1, L-1, E, OPT, STEM-OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.).

What You'll Do

  • Special Projects: Lead special projects that test and strengthen new advocacy approaches to advance maternal and child survival, including:
    • Sports advocacy model: Lead development of a strategic approach to better leverage sport to advance maternal and child survival. Support the operationalization of new ideas and engagement models, connecting efforts and learning across IRPP markets.
    • Global political coalition: Lead an emerging initiative to build a new global political coalition in support of maternal and child survival through a new partnership. Help shape the advocacy approach, develop relationships with new champions, and connect the initiative to foundation and market priorities.
    • Supporting emerging AI global governance advocacy partnerships
  • Partner across the foundation: Build effective working relationships with program, policy, communications, and other relevant teams to bring technical expertise and market insight together, align priorities, and coordinate contributions to shared work.
  • Understand foundation priorities: Work with program and issue advocacy teams to understand the global development challenges the foundation seeks to address, the solutions set out in its strategies, and their intended impact, drawing on technical expertise across the foundation.
  • Assess market context: Work with Canada and UN leads to assess the political economy, institutional mandates, priorities, capabilities, and constraints shaping each market, including Canadian interests and the forward-looking agenda of the UN ecosystem in New York.
  • Translate into market opportunities: Bring these analyses together with market leads to identify how each market could advance foundation priorities and the expected impact of its contributions. Develop market-specific policy proposals, arguments, and concrete asks with relevant foundation teams, supporting market leads in developing their advocacy approaches.
  • Support broader policy and development architecture work: Partner with the Deputy Director on broader policy and development architecture questions, i.e. global cooperation trends, system reforms, etc., examining how global trends and institutional changes affect foundation priorities and the roles IRPP markets can play.
  • Partner and Contract Management: Engage and manage external partners and consultants supporting these workstreams. Develop scopes of work, manage contracts, oversee deliverables and budgets, and coordinate with relevant internal teams to ensure work remains aligned with agreed objectives.


Your Experience

  • 10+ years of experience in advocacy, government relations, public policy, multilateral engagement, or strategy, ideally in a nonprofit, governmental, philanthropic, or international setting. An advanced degree is a plus.
  • Demonstrated experience translating complex global health or development strategies into clear policy arguments, market-specific asks, and practical advocacy approaches, combining broad policy understanding with the ability to engage deeply with technical subjects.
  • Proven ability to craft big-picture strategic direction while developing and executing flexible, practical implementation plans.
  • Experience engaging external partners and managing contracts, including scopes of work, budgets, timelines, and deliverables.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with an ability to synthesize complex concepts, evidence, political context, and recommendations succinctly and persuasively.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead ambiguous or emerging workstreams, assess competing priorities, and deliver high-quality analysis and products for multiple internal collaborators.
  • Knowledge of global health, Canada’s development policy and political ecosystem, and the UN system would be an asset.
  • Highly collaborative, and low ego

*Must have unrestricted work authorization in the country where this position is located. The Foundation does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. This includes direct company sponsorship and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (eg: H-1B, O-1, L-1, E, OPT, STEM-OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.).

The salary range for this role is $212,800 to $329,800 USD. We recognize high-wage market differences in Seattle, WA and Washington D.C., where our offices are located. The range for this role in these locations is $234,000 to $362,800 USD. As a mission-driven organization, we strive to balance competitive pay with our mission. New hires salaries are typically between the range minimum and the salary range midpoint. Actual placement in the range will depend on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, and expertise, as evaluated during the interview process.

title: Growth Associate
description:
Growth at CFO Insights

The world’s most demanding investors are busy managing trillions, and ignore anything average. Are you excited by the challenge of making them act?

Are you looking to work in an exceptional entrepreneurial team with ambitious, motivated and extremely driven people? And do you want real ownership from your first week? If so, now is the time to apply for the Growth role at Private Equity Insights.

The mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors.

You will work in sprints and get fast execution under your skin. AI has completely changed the game: You will learn to deploy it to outperform a marketing team of 20+ people, while also learning the fundamentals of copywriting that makes elite investors act, get it to the right investor at a meaningful frequency and deploy what works across every marketing channel.

If you want an ambitious mission, real ownership and the fastest learning curve of your career: apply.

Why CFO Insights

CFO Insights is Northern Europe’s largest CFO forum and aims to connect and develop CFOs, finance leaders, and tomorrow's innovators by addressing the issues of the future CFO. We are connecting more than 11,000 professionals from more than 15 countries.

CFO Insights is part of United Media which focuses on building large scale industry media and conferences products in sectors such as insurance, HR, private equity, retail, etc. As of today, we have organically launched 8 media companies and acquired one.

What we offer you

  • Master the highest bar in the world. Our audience is the world's most demanding investors. They ignore anything average. If your work can make them act, you can make anyone act.
  • Unlimited growth potential. You will get responsibility before you feel ready. That is how you grow fast. We strongly believe in and have a track record of promoting internally. You can expect coaching and development from leaders, peers and experts.
  • Skills that compound for life. Fast execution, copywriting, pricing, conversion optimisation, structured problem solving, and the ability to create impact anywhere in the business at scale.
  • Ownership from the very start. You own outcomes, not tasks. We agree the goal, and you find the way.
  • Travel opportunity. You will be joining our 10+ conferences.

What you will do

Responsibilities in this job will vary, however, feed into the mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors. They will be mostly centered around the following:

  • Build the audience. Identify, target, and convert every fund into our community, and make sure each one receives the right message, at the right time, and never one too many.
  • Own marketing channels that drive revenue. Through existing and new marketing channels, you execute activities that ultimately will drive revenue
  • Write copy that persuades. Every email, landing page and post. Become the best copywriter and leverage it at scale with AI.
  • Sprint, test, implement. Measure the impact of all experiments you run, test offers, copy, prices and pages until the numbers move.
  • Build systems, not one-offs. Anything you do twice becomes a playbook or an AI workflow, so the next win takes less effort than the last.
  • Do whatever it takes to win. Some days that means designing an AI workflow. Some days it means checking investors in at the registration desk at 7am. Nobody here is too good for the work that deliver value for investors and fund managers.

What we expect from you

  • 1 to 3 years of experience
  • Min. a bachelor or master degree with great results
  • A UK work permit. We do not sponsor visas.
  • Strong work ethic with a sense of urgency
  • Exceptional drive and desire to be the best at what you do
  • Proactive approach and sense of ownership/responsibility of everything you do
  • A humble approach and share our passion for building companies and developing people
  • Interested in continuous learning and proactively searching for ways to optimise

Practical details

Full-time, in person from our London office (WeWork), 5 days a week. Expect to travel for work about 20 days a year. The start date is flexible.

title: PT/OT Tech - PRN
description:
At Cleveland Clinic Health System, we believe in a better future for healthcare. And each of us is responsible for honoring our commitment to excellence, pushing the boundaries and transforming the patient experience, every day.

We all have the power to help, heal and change lives — beginning with our own. That’s the power of the Cleveland Clinic Health System team, and The Power of Every One.

Job Title

PT/OT Tech - PRN

Location

Cleveland

Facility

Cleveland Clinic Main Campus

Department

Physical Therapy Hosp-Neurological Institute

Job Code

C12004

Shift

Days

Schedule

8:00am-4:30pm

Job Summary

Job Details


Join Cleveland Clinic’s Main Campus where research and surgery are advanced, technology is leading-edge, patient care is world-class, and caregivers are family. Cleveland Clinic is recognized as one of the top hospitals in the country. You will work alongside passionate and dedicated caregivers, receive endless support and appreciation, and build a rewarding career with one of the most respected healthcare organizations in the world.

As a Physical or Occupational Therapy Technician, you will assist licensed therapy professionals by supporting patients with lifting, transferring, gait training, and exercise activities, while providing therapeutic assistance as directed. This Rehab Technician position plays a vital role in helping our Physical and Occupational Therapists deliver patient care across both our critical care units and regular nursing floors. It serves as an excellent entry point into the healthcare field, offering valuable hands-on experience and opportunities for professional skill development.


This position is well-suited for individuals seeking practical, hands-on experience in a therapy-centered environment prior to pursuing advanced education in nursing, physical therapy, or other healthcare professions. While some team members choose to build long-term careers in this role, many utilize it as a valuable steppingstone toward advanced clinical pathways.

This is a PRN role. A caregiver in this position will work 2 weekend days per month. Other days are available to be picked up during the week in addition to the required 2 weekend days.

A caregiver who excels in this role will:

  • Maintain sanitary, orderly conditions in department.
  • Inventory departmental equipment.
  • Ensure equipment is in good working order.
  • Fabricate equipment as directed.
  • Perform set-up of patient-related equipment.

Minimum qualifications for the ideal future caregiver include:

  • High School Diploma/GED
  • Basic Life Support (BLS) certification through the American Heart Association (AHA) or the American Red Cross
  • Familiar with performing job-related tasks, such as reading labels and instructions and completing order forms
  • Basic mathematical skills sufficient to support inventory management, item measurement, equipment preparation, and supply ordering within budget guidelines

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to walk without assistive device and to maintain balance despite sudden load in order to support patient from falling during gait training.
  • Ability to lift and reach with arms sufficiently to lift patient's arm and leg during therapeutic treatment program.
  • Sensation of touch and manual dexterity to be able to palpate muscle tension or to monitor patient pulse.
  • Visual acuity to observe patient's gross and fine motor movements in order to analyze these movements.
  • Ability to speak clearly enough to instruct patients and families who may not be able to read. Ability to hear or understand patient's description of symptoms and response to treatment.
  • Mental ability to interpret clinical data for the establishment and implementation of appropriate patient treatment.
  • Ability to identify and resolve problems using critical thinking and decision-making.

Personal Protective Equipment:

  • Follows standard precautions using personal protective equipment as required.

The policy of Cleveland Clinic Health System and its system hospitals (Cleveland Clinic Health System) is to provide equal opportunity to all of our caregivers and applicants for employment in our drug free environment. All offers of employment are followed by testing for controlled substances.

Cleveland Clinic Health System administers an influenza prevention program. You will be required to comply with this program, which will include obtaining an influenza vaccination on an annual basis or obtaining an approved exemption.

Decisions concerning employment, transfers and promotions are made upon the basis of the best qualified candidate without regard to color, race, religion, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, ancestry, status as a disabled or Vietnam era veteran or any other characteristic protected by law. Information provided on this application may be shared with any Cleveland Clinic Health System facility.

If applying for a Florida position, please see the following website for more information on the background screening requirements required by the Agency of Health Care Administration:

Please review the Equal Employment Opportunity poster.

Cleveland Clinic is pleased to be an equal employment opportunity employer.

title: Senior Manager of Development Operations
description:
· Lead the Development Operations function and establish policies, procedures, service standards, and best practices for gift processing, donor data management, reporting, analysis, and operational controls.

· Supervise, coach, and mentor Data Processing Manager, Development Operations Specialists, Coordinator, Gift Specialist, and other assigned staff; establish clear expectations, priorities, accountability, cross-training, and backup coverage.

· Oversee the timely and accurate processing of charitable gifts and pledges, including checks, securities, gifts-in-kind, matching gifts, credit card activity, recurring gifts, grants, online gifts, donor-advised funds, wires, bequests, and restricted gifts.

· Ensure timely and accurate donor acknowledgements, tax receipts, pledge documentation, constituent updates, and other required correspondence.

· Maintain overall database integrity through routine audits, data-quality reviews, duplicate management, coding standards, system checks, and documented corrective action.

· Establish and monitor daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual controls for gift processing, recurring activity, deposits, imports, reconciliations, exceptions, aging items, and backlogs.

· Ensure controls have clearly documented owners, backups, deadlines, evidence of completion, escalation requirements, and management review.

· Lead timely reconciliation of Development records to Finance records; research and resolve discrepancies involving gift coding, restrictions, deposits, revenue tracking, and donor records.

· Oversee recurring Development Operations exception reviews, including unresolved vendor items, system issues, manual workarounds, interface failures, missed transactions, and aging items requiring resolution.

· Identify trends, unusual activity, missing activity, or process breakdowns and ensure issues are investigated, documented, resolved, and escalated promptly when appropriate.

· Identify and recommend opportunities for automation, process improvement, reduced manual entry, and improved cross-department workflows; partner with Data Management on system enhancements and integration needs affecting Development Operations.

· Ensure compliance with applicable accounting, tax, privacy, ethical fundraising, gift acceptance, and donor-record requirements.

· Promote a culture of ownership, urgency, accuracy, continuous improvement, customer service, and collaborative problem-solving.

title: Specialist II, Audit & Advisory (IT and Cybersecurity Audit)
description:
TransUnion's Job Applicant Privacy Notice

Team Overview

The Global Audit & Advisory (GAA) function is an independent and objective assurance and advisory organization that helps strengthen governance, risk management, and internal controls across the enterprise. The India Global Capability Center (GCC) serves as a strategic extension of the global GAA organization, providing audit and advisory support across the United States, United Kingdom, APAC, Africa, and Global business functions.
The IT & Cybersecurity team within GAA GCC partners with global stakeholders to assess technology and cybersecurity risks, evaluate the effectiveness of controls, and provide insights that support business resiliency and regulatory compliance. The team executes audits and advisory engagements covering cybersecurity, cloud technologies, infrastructure, identity and access management, vulnerability management, SDLC, data protection, disaster recovery, and emerging technology initiatives.
This role offers exposure to a broad range of technologies, cybersecurity domains, cloud platforms, and business initiatives, providing significant opportunities for professional growth and global stakeholder engagement.

This is a hybrid position and involves regular performance of job responsibilities virtually as well as in-person at an assigned TU office location for a minimum of two days a week.

Role Overview And Core Responsibilities

  • Support the planning and execution of IT and cybersecurity audits, advisory reviews, and risk assessments.
  • Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of IT and cybersecurity controls across applications, infrastructure, databases, networks, and cloud environments.
  • Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of IT General Controls (ITGCs), cybersecurity controls, and technology governance processes.
  • Assess key areas including cybersecurity, access management, cloud security, incident management, business continuity, disaster recovery, and system implementations.
  • Perform control testing, analyze results, and document audit conclusions and observations.
  • Prepare audit reports and communicate risks, control gaps, and remediation recommendations to stakeholders.
  • Communicate observations, control weaknesses, and associated risks to stakeholders in a clear and professional manner.
  • Where appropriate, lead portions of engagements and facilitate discussions regarding remediation actions and risk mitigation strategies.
  • Track and monitor remediation activities for open audit findings and validate the implementation of corrective actions.
  • Stay informed of emerging cybersecurity threats, industry trends, and leading practices, while contributing to departmental initiatives and continuous improvement efforts.
  • Build and maintain effective relationships with global stakeholders while preserving audit independence
  • Participate in departmental initiatives, special projects, knowledge-sharing activities, and continuous improvement efforts that support GAA objectives and strategic priorities

Required Knowledge And Experiences

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related field.
  • 3-7 years of experience in IT Audit, IT Risk, IT Assurance, or Information Security, including at least 2 years with a public accounting or professional services firm.
  • Strong understanding of IT and cybersecurity frameworks, including NIST, CIS Controls, ISO 27001, and COBIT.
  • Knowledge of key information security domains, including governance and risk management, access management, cloud security, network security, security architecture, application security, incident management, and business continuity/disaster recovery.
  • Experience assessing IT and cybersecurity controls across on-premises and cloud environments, with a solid understanding of infrastructure, operating systems, databases, networking, and vulnerability management.
  • Familiarity with security and governance tools such as Splunk, SailPoint IIQ, BMC Remedy, and audit management tools such as Optro (formerly AuditBoard).
  • Strong analytical, risk assessment, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Self-motivated and adaptable, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, and respond effectively to changing business needs.
  • Professional certification such as CISA or CISSP required.

The role helps ensure that platforms remain stable, secure, reliable and performant while supporting their continued improvement through platform enhancements, automation and integrations.

title: GRC Analyst
description:
Help make the world more hospitable

The hospitality industry is uniquely human, and it deserves technology that’s just as inspiring as the people behind it. At Mews, we’re transforming the industry with a platform that helps hotels run smarter, move faster and create better guest experiences.

You’ll work with smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do. You’ll have autonomy and the trust to make good decisions and move quickly. And you’ll enjoy a real sense of purpose as you see the impact of what we’re building.

If you’re motivated by ownership, curiosity and meaningful impact, and are driven to deliver consistent high performance, you’ll feel at home here.

About the role

Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:

You will own the governance, risk and compliance work that lets Mews prove to hotels and large buyers that guest and card data is safe. Hotel groups ask for proof before they sign, and that proof comes from audits, certifications and vendor reviews. This is a new role in our IT and Security team, and a good moment to join, because ISO 27001, SOC 2 and PCI DSS now sit at the centre of how Mews wins large customers.

You will work in the IT and Security team, you will make the final call on each review, run risk assessments, keep policies up to date and gather evidence for auditors. You own your tasks from start to finish, and you work with teams across Mews and with external auditors.

Mews looks after private guest and card data for hotels. Audit season starts every January, and vendor reviews arrive all year. The work needs someone who judges risk clearly, follows up with busy owners and closes every gap. Our compliance tool (Vanta) is new, so you will help shape how the process works.

What you would do

  • Run vendor security reviews from start to decision, and make the final risk call on each one

  • Run risk assessments and follow every gap until it is closed

  • Keep company policies current and collect evidence for ISO 27001, SOC 2 and PCI DSS audits, working with auditors and control owners

  • Use AI to redesign parts of the review and evidence process, for example drafting first-pass vendor assessments and matching controls to evidence

  • Write down the AI-supported approaches you build so teammates can reuse them, and check every AI output against the source before it reaches an audit file

AI Fluency Level 3: In this role, that means you have already changed how a GRC or compliance process works using AI, for example how vendor questionnaires are read or how evidence is collected, and not only made your own tasks faster. You have built an approach that colleagues now follow. You check AI output against the source (a vendor report, a control, a policy) every time, because an audit file cannot hold a wrong answer.

For more information on AI fluency at Mews, please refer to AI Fluency at Mews: A Comprehensive Guide for Candidates on Confluence.

What you would bring

  • About 3 years in GRC, IT audit, compliance or information security [TBC: to confirm with the Hiring Manager]

  • Hands-on work in ISO 27001, SOC 2 or PCI DSS audits, not only theory

  • Experience running vendor risk reviews or risk assessments on your own, from start to decision

  • Clear written English, and the ability to get evidence on time from busy teams

  • AI Fluency Level 3 or the equivalent hands-on experience, shown in how you have used AI in GRC work

Nice to have

  • Experience with a GRC tool such as Vanta, Drata or OneTrust

  • A certificate such as ISO 27001 Lead Implementer, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, CISA or CISM

  • Regulatory work such as GDPR, DORA, NIS2 or EMI

867 000 Kč—1 240 000 Kč CZK

Pay Transparency at Mews

Salary ranges are provided in good faith and reflect current market conditions and internal pay structures. Final compensation may be adjusted based on funding, budget constraints, or exceptional candidate qualifications, but will remain within reasonable proximity to the stated range.

This salary disclosure is provided in compliance with applicable pay transparency legislation. We are committed to equal pay practices and prohibit salary history inquiries during our recruitment process.

If the location you're applying from wasn't originally advertised for this role, salary range information is available upon request at any point during the application/interview process - your recruiter will be able to help.

What’s in it for you?

Our success is powered by our incredible people, supported by benefits that help them thrive.

Global benefits

No matter where you’re based, you’ll enjoy:

  • Unlimited paid holiday (yes, really)
  • Participation in our company share program
  • Paid parental leave (6 months fully paid for primary caregivers, 2 months for secondary, available after one year of service)
  • An annual Learning budget of €300 (and more for high performers) to support your development
  • Monthly "EDGE" time to Explore, Develop, Grow, and Elevate yourself
  • A work from anywhere policy with flexibility to work abroad for a few weeks each year
  • Relocation options, available after one year
  • Flexible, hybrid working options
  • A home office setup budget to make your workspace your own and a monthly work-from-home allowance
  • Claude tokens, so you can automate workflows and build smarter, more efficient ways of working

Local benefits

You'll receive additional benefits that vary by location, from healthcare and retirement plans to team events, socials and other perks. Ask us about it during your interview process.

Life at Mews

We’re an equal opportunities employer. We value teams that reflect the diversity of the customers and communities we serve. Different perspectives make better ideas, stronger products and a more welcoming company.

We also believe transparency is important when deciding if you're the right fit. Mews is an ambitious, high-pressure environment of continuous learning and high standards. Success here requires resilience, adaptability and a willingness to solve difficult problems.

A few things that define how we work:

  • High autonomy means high responsibility. People are expected to take ownership and drive outcomes. There isn’t a detailed playbook for everything, and that’s part of what makes the work challenging – and rewarding.
  • Change is constant. We’re growing quickly and adapting as we scale. Teams, processes and priorities continue to evolve, and only people who stay curious and agile will thrive.
  • We’re remote-first, not relationship-free. Flexibility is core to how we work, but strong relationships still matter. Our teams are global, so we need expert collaborators and communicators to help us move forward together.
  • AI is an integral part of our processes. It’s not here to steal people’s jobs, but to amplify efficiency and productivity. We’re motivated to proactively use the technology to seek out better ways of working and share our findings with the rest of the company.

If there's anything we can do to support you during the application process, let us know.

We don't discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, nationality, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other protected characteristic.

One final thing: don't hold back. If you don't meet 100% of the criteria in this job description but you're certain you could make a big impact, apply. Everyone should have equal access to opportunities, and we're committed to providing an inclusive experience.

If Mews sounds like the kind of environment where you'd thrive, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Director, Global Program Advocacy and Communications, Health
description:
The Foundation

We are the largest nonprofit fighting poverty, disease, and inequity around the world. Founded on a simple premise: people everywhere, regardless of identity or circumstances, should have the chance to live healthy, productive lives. We believe our employees should reflect the rich diversity of the global populations we aim to serve. We provide an exceptional benefits package to employees and their families which include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with no premiums, generous paid time off, paid family leave, foundation-paid retirement contribution, regional holidays, and opportunities to engage in several employee communities. As a workplace, we’re committed to creating an environment for you to thrive both personally and professionally.

The Team

The mission of the Global Policy & Advocacy (GPA) division is to understand and shape the public policy debates affecting the foundation's work, build support for its major program and policy objectives, and develop partnerships and alliances that can advance the foundation's objectives nationally and globally. Because the foundation's resources alone are not enough to solve the challenges ahead, GPA also supports advocacy efforts to engage diverse collaborators and promote innovative solutions that advance our program goals. We work in close partnership with grantees, our colleagues in the Global Health, Global Development, Global Growth & Opportunity, U.S. and Gender Equality programs and Communications to build the environment in which all people have the opportunity to lead healthy and productive lives.

Global Program Advocacy & Communications (GPAC) is the Foundation’s global capability for issue advocacy and communications. GPAC engages where work is cross-market, technically complex, and requires global assets and specialized expertise. Working with our program, regional, and country teams, we help mobilize the financing, policy change, and public legitimacy required for impact. GPAC’s core functions include:

• Translating program priorities into advocacy strategies and asks: Applying deep issue knowledge and policy expertise to translate technical program goals into actionable policy and financing priorities.
• Developing and synthesizing evidence to influence decision-makers: Investing in and translating research, data, and technical evidence into investment cases, policy content, and market-ready materials.
• Building and mobilizing advocacy ecosystems: Convening and aligning partners, coalitions, and champions to advance policy change, influence agendas, mobilize resources, and strengthen accountability.
• Leading global issue communications: Developing evidence-based narratives and communications assets; supporting strategic media engagement and campaigns; and anticipating and managing communications and reputational risks.
• Providing specialized advocacy expertise: Offering strategic counsel on complex advocacy challenges to build enabling policy, regulatory, and communications environments.
• Facilitating cross-team collaboration and learning: Connecting program, policy, communications, regional, and country teams; sharing intelligence on emerging risks and opportunities; and translating learnings across geographies.

GPAC partners with Foundation colleagues and external stakeholders—including governments, multilateral institutions, civil society, philanthropy, the media, and others—to ensure that global strategies strengthen country-led advocacy and drive measurable progress.

Your Role
The global health sector is being redefined. Development assistance for health has decreased significantly since its peak in 2021, major health multilaterals had difficulty meeting replenishment targets, and bilateral donors are shifting their funding approaches. At the same time, governments in Africa and Asia are raising domestic health spending and asserting leadership through the Lusaka Agenda, the Accra Reset, Africa CDC, AUDA NEPAD, the African Medicines Agency, and India’s growing role as a source of vaccines, digital public infrastructure and AI for other countries. AI is moving from pilots into public health systems. The Foundation has committed to spend its resources by 2045 to help ensure no mother, child or baby dies of a preventable cause, the next generation grows up in a world without deadly infectious diseases, and hundreds of millions of people break free from poverty.


The Director, Global Program Advocacy and Communications (Global PAC), Health leads the Foundation’s global health advocacy through this transition. The Director provides strategic leadership for the team that turns the Foundation’s health priorities into political will, financing and policy change, and helps build a system of health financing and policy that countries own and that will last beyond any single donor, including the Foundation.


The Director leads Global PAC Health, including the Program Partner teams aligned to the Global Health, Global Development and Gender Equality divisions, and Health Communications. The team’s centralized capabilities drive global outcomes and create the narratives, global public goods, evidence, and specialized policy capacity that make market- and country-led advocacy more effective. This includes building investment cases with program and finance and resource mobilization teams, building partner coalitions, crafting issue narratives and spotting risks, and strengthening the policy and regulatory environments needed to advance our health financing and policy goals. The team’s work supports the Foundation’s goals and the GPA division priorities that advance them: Maternal & Child Survival, Health Research and Development (R&D), Innovation Introduction, and Health Financing.


The Director works across the Foundation with the program strategy teams (PSTs) and division leadership teams, and across GPA with the market-led teams in Europe, Middle East and East Asia (EMEEA), North America (NAT), Africa, India and South/Southeast Asia, the Development Policy and Finance (DPAF) team, and the philanthropic partnership team (PPT), so that Foundation priorities reach decision-makers through strategic, coordinated advocacy. The Director leads the team that serves as GPA’s front door to the PSTs and division leadership and aligns GPA’s advocacy capabilities behind the Foundation’s highest-impact priorities.


Global and country teams each hold something the other needs. Seattle sits close to PSTs, government relations teams in donor capital are close to financing decisions, and regional and country teams hold the context, and the relationship with governments in our delivery geographies The Director makes the partnership model between global and regional/country teams work: co-designing strategy with Africa and India colleagues from the outset, sharing intelligence in both directions, advocating inside the Foundation for country priorities with PSTs and division leaders, and leading GPAC Health on the connections and priorities a global team is best placed to do.


The ideal leader understands and translates complex PST strategies and brings the best of GPA to them: its relationships, intelligence, financing expertise and communications capability. They have deep advocacy experience, strong knowledge of financing sources across bilateral, multilateral and philanthropic funders and the ability to work with the Resource Mobilization (RM) Hub and other GPA teams to maximize resource mobilization. They understand how health systems are financed and run, how ministries of finance and health make budget decisions, and how to effect policy change at global, regional and national levels. They have earned credibility with leaders in governments and institutions across the Global South. They are both a practitioner and an orchestrator: credible enough to speak in specifics on advocacy tactics, strategy and partners, and skilled at keeping many complex, interdependent efforts moving at once. They are decisive, with the credibility to define clearly what is and is not achievable and to bring colleagues with them. This role suits a leader who has worked in multiple parts of global health, in or with government, in multilateral, academic or research institutions, in civil society, or in industry.


This role partners with the Director, Global PAC Global Growth and Opportunity (GGO) to co-lead the overall Global PAC team and reports to the President, GPA.


*Applications accepted until Friday, November 27th. Locations considered for this role are Seattle, WA, Washington, DC and London, UK. As a global search for the best talent, all qualified senior leaders are encouraged to apply.

What You'll Do


Strategy and leadership

  • Set and implement the Global PAC Health strategy. Define where Global PAC Health engages focusing on cross-market, technically complex or politically sensitive work and on reusable global assets that regional and country teams draw on. Own the quality of the strategy and the delivery of its outcomes.
  • Lead through the GPA division priorities. Own Global PAC Health’s contribution to the division priorities on Maternal & Child Survival, Health R&D, Innovation Introduction and Health Financing, turning each priority into an integrated plan that links advocacy, financing, policy and communications. Work with the relevant PSTs, regional and country advocacy teams, and GPA colleagues to set one clear strategy and ask for each priority, align the partners, coalitions and donors needed to deliver it, and use key global moments to build political commitment and mobilize resources. Hold the team accountable for measurable progress, and make sure global efforts reinforce the work of country and regional teams.
  • Be a strategic partner to PSTs and serve as a bridge to GPA teams. Develop a deep understanding of each PST’s strategy and lead the Program Partner leaders who represent GPA on PST and division leadership teams. Bring the best of GPA to program teams in a coordinated way, translating technical priorities into clear policy and financing asks, meeting each team where it is while holding the line on what advocacy can and cannot achieve. Bring regional and country perspectives into PST strategy early, before asks are set. Bring hands-on advocacy expertise to sharpen the team’s engagement and strengthen the credibility of GPA’s counsel.

Partnership with regional and country teams

  • Build one strategy with Africa and India. Co-design advocacy strategies, asks, and plans with the Africa Policy, Government Relations and Partnerships (PGRP) and India PAC teams from the start. Clarify roles between GPAC, regional and country teams in Africa and India, and government relationships teams in donor markets. Share intelligence in both directions and hold joint accountability for results.
  • Carry country evidence and leadership into global decisions. Provide space in global platforms for analysis and champions from the regional/country efforts, including through replenishments and global moments such as the G20, the UN General Assembly and the World Health Assembly.
  • Broker South-South exchange. Work with the India and Africa teams to spread proven approaches across countries, including, AI tools, regulatory reform, local manufacturing when economically viable, and to support the growing role of India and African countries as suppliers of health innovation to other low- and middle-income countries.

Financing, architecture and ecosystems

  • Drive policy and financing alignment for health PST priorities. Define the policy and financing asks for PST issues and lead PAC’s contribution to replenishments, pledging moments and deal teams, coordinating advocacy, strengthening positioning and aligning partners and communications. Work within the GPA Resource Mobilization (RM) Hub model: partner with the GPA teams who lead funder relationships, opportunity development and deal brokerage, and with the RM Hub on shared visibility of financing needs and sources, deal ownership and escalation.
  • Advocate for financing countries own health systems. With DPAF, the RM Hub and regional teams, support the shift from aid dependence toward domestic resource mobilization, stronger budget execution, and blended and innovative finance. Engage multilateral development banks and newer sources of finance, including Gulf and Asian governments and domestic and diaspora philanthropy.
  • Help shape the reform of global health architecture. Help the Foundation take clear, constructive positions as global health initiatives, UN agencies and donors reorganize, consistent with the Lusaka Agenda and country-led platforms. Promote one national plan, one budget and one accountability framework in each country. Engage bilateral donors as they move to compact-based models so new agreements reinforce national systems.
  • Shape the global health advocacy ecosystem and build coalitions. Steward a focused portfolio of health advocacy partners, guide PAC’s engagement with disease-specific institutions and communities, and maintain accountability for results. Convene multilateral institutions, civil society and philanthropic partners around shared goals, and build the investment cases, convenings and cross-market learning that make country and regional advocacy more effective.
  • Lead advocacy and partnerships on AI for health. With PSTs, the Africa and India teams and GPA colleagues, advance the policy, financing and governance needed to move proven AI tools from pilots into government-owned health systems: lower costs and clear procurement pathways, the data and compute foundations low- and middle-income countries need, and standards for safety, equity and evidence. Use AI to make GPAC’s own advocacy and communications faster and better informed.

Issue communications

  • Lead issue communications. Oversee Health Communications, developing evidence-based narratives and communication assets, supporting strategic media engagement and campaigns, and in partnership with the Communications division and regional teams, manage communications and reputational risks associated with the issue portfolio.
  • Make the case for health as an investment in growth. With the GGO team, show how health, nutrition and human capital drive productivity, jobs and economic growth, in terms finance ministers and investors use.

Co-leading Global PAC

  • Partner with the Director, Global PAC GGO to set shared direction, operating model and standards for Global PAC, align budget and portfolio decisions, and co-lead portfolio and strategy reviews.
  • Drive innovation and learning in advocacy. Pilot new advocacy approaches, narratives and engagement models, measure results, including value for money and the defense of past gains, document what works and what does not, and share learning across PAC and GPA to build PAC as a center of excellence.

People leadership

  • Lead and develop the team. Set a clear vision and a high bar for performance. Lead, coach and grow leaders and individual contributors across time zones and geographies. Hire and onboard talent, set clear expectations, give and seek feedback, support development, and hold people accountable. Build an inclusive, energized team culture and lead people with care and clarity through organizational change.

Your Experience

  • A master’s degree or equivalent demonstrated experience, preferably in public policy, public health, health economics, international relations or international development.
  • 15+ years of progressive, senior-level experience leading and developing senior teams and leading policy, advocacy and financing initiatives in global health and global development, or equivalent, preferably across government, multilateral, academic, non-profit and private sectors.
  • Experience working in or with governments in low- and middle-income countries, ideally in Africa or South Asia, and with multilateral agencies, development banks and global health institutions.
  • Professional or lived experience of health systems in low- and middle-income countries, and credibility with leaders of governments and institutions in the Global South.
  • Deep knowledge of health financing and health systems: how budgets are set, released and spent, how domestic resource mobilization works, and how global health initiatives finance and deliver programs.
  • Demonstrated record of mobilizing resources across bilateral, multilateral, development bank and philanthropic funders, ideally in global health.
  • Mastery-level expertise in advocacy and influencing related to resource mobilization, policy analysis, communications, coalition building, and partnership development with diverse constituencies, including the private sector, policymakers, civil society, academia, multilateral agencies and development banks. Campaign or strategic communications experience is an asset.
  • Proven ability to turn data, economic analysis and implementation evidence into investment cases and policy proposals decision-makers act on.
  • Hands-on advocacy credibility: able to speak in specifics on advocacy tactics, strategy and partners, and to steer multiple complex, interdependent workstreams at once while keeping command of the detail.
  • Strategy development and execution, including impact measurement, portfolio management and prioritization in a changing resource environment.
  • Working knowledge of digital public infrastructure, data and AI, and the policy, financing and governance questions they raise for health systems.
  • Ability to learn technical health subject matter quickly, earn the respect of PSTs and technical and program experts, and navigate complex, politically sensitive environments.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, and the ability to translate technical program strategy into clear, compelling asks for different audiences and cultures. Professional working proficiency in French or Portuguese is an asset.
  • Proven ability to build trusted relationships and drive outcomes inside a complex, matrixed organization: someone who defines clearly what can and cannot be achieved, and challenges senior colleagues constructively while preserving the partnership.
  • Excellent leadership, judgment, intellectual curiosity and diplomacy, with the ability to hold the line while meeting partners where they are, to lead through influence, and to build, lead and develop high-performing, inclusive teams, including through moments of change.
  • Willingness to travel a minimum of 30%, much of it in Africa and Asia.

title: Engineering Manager - North American Sports
description:
At Hudl, we build great teams. We hire the best of the best to ensure you’re working with people you can constantly learn from. You’re trusted to get your work done your way while testing the limits of what’s possible and what’s next. We work hard to provide a culture where everyone feels supported, and our employees feel it—their votes helped us become one of the Top 100 Inspiring Workplaces.

We think of ourselves as the team behind the team, supporting the lifelong impact sports can have: the lessons in teamwork and dedication; the influence of inspiring coaches; and the opportunities to reach new heights. That’s why we help teams from all over the world see their game differently. Our products make it easier for coaches and athletes at any level to capture video, analyze data, share highlights and more.

Ready to join us?

Your Role

We’re hiring an Engineering Manager to join our North American Sports (NAS) squad within the College & Professional group, leading squads that deliver products and services to coaches and athletes across American Football, Basketball, Ice Hockey, Soccer and Volleyball. NAS focuses on the top clubs and athletes in the industry and works closely with them to optimize their workflows in our unified ecosystem across web and mutli-device platforms. As an Engineering Manager, you’ll:

  • Lead with technical excellence. You’ll work closely with engineers to make sure we’re building high-quality, scalable software the right way, and you’ll be involved in architecture and system design.
  • Drive product delivery. You’ll partner with product managers, design and QA to understand customer and business value, negotiate trade-offs, and oversee the successful shipment of new features in a fast-paced environment.
  • Empower your team. You’ll typically manage 6/8 engineers across two squads, focusing on their growth and wellbeing while building a high-performing, healthy team culture.
  • Champion AI-first engineering. We’re heavily invested in an AI-first mindset. You’ll encourage your team to use AI tools and modern tech to stay ahead of the curve, and you’ll help shape what we share more widely across Hudl.
  • Help unify the Hudl platform. This role succeeds when College & Professional workflows land cleanly in core Hudl tools and customers get one coherent experience. You’ll measure success by the workflows converged and the customer outcomes unlocked.

Location

For this role, we're currently considering candidates who are within commuting distance of our office in London.

Must-Haves

  • Experienced. You have 3+ years of experience in engineering management, ideally with a background as an individual contributor or tech lead on customer-facing product teams. Platform or API experience is valued alongside it.
  • Product-minded. You’ve shipped user-facing software and can partner with product, design and QA to weigh customer value against technical trade-offs. You’re comfortable owning delivery in a fast-paced environment.
  • Technically grounded. You have a strong technical background and are comfortable architecting complex software, ideally with C#, TypeScript, AWS and a relational database such as PostgreSQL. You can stay involved in system design and architecture decisions.

title: Co-op, LNP Discovery
description:
Company Overview:

Strand Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering programmable mRNA therapeutics to unlock the full potential of genetic medicines. Strand is applying its proprietary Signal Stack platform, which integrates EverScript circular RNA, AmpliScript self-replicating RNA, SignalPath targeted delivery, and logic-driven SignalLock genetic circuits to enable precise control of therapeutic activity across tissues and cell types and overcome foundational limitations in targeting, durability, and safety.

Strand is advancing a pipeline with an initial focus on oncology and autoimmune disease. Its initial program, STX-001, an intratumorally delivered LNP-encapsulated self-replicating RNA expressing IL-12, has demonstrated preliminary evidence of systemic immune activation and anti-tumor activity in patients with advanced solid tumors who have progressed on prior therapies. Building on this early clinical validation, intravenously delivered STX-003 is designed for tumor-targeted expression and avoidance of off-target expression. STX-003, which is expected to enter the clinic in mid-2026, has the potential to be a major step forward for the fields of genetic medicine and oncology. Strand is also advancing STX-005, an in vivo CAR-T program designed to enable controlled, durable expression and repeat dosing. Founded by MIT synthetic biology pioneers, Strand has raised over $250 million and is headquartered in Boston, MA.

Become the next standout single strand!

Job Summary:

Strand is looking for people who have the enthusiasm and motivation to be a highly contributing member of a small but extremely productive team. This opportunity will offer the employee the ability to work in a matrix-based environment and be a part of the future strategy of the company.

We are looking for a highly motivated and innovative candidate for the role of Co-op, LNP Discovery. This is a fantastic opportunity to make a significant impact as a scientifically motivated self-starter capable of independently conceiving, conducting, and critically analyzing his/her own work with minimal supervision.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Executing formulation related experiments including preparing, optimizing, and characterizing the LNP formulations.
  • Carrying out some bioassays for evaluating the LNP formulations.
  • Facilitating general lab techniques such as sample preparation, cell culture, and nucleic acid work.
  • Working across diverse areas to support the group's research activities in a fast-paced and collaborative environment.

Qualifications:

  • On track to graduate with a B.S. or M.S. in Biology, Biochemistry, Bioengineering, or a related discipline.
  • Coursework related to dosage forms, drug/gene delivery system, and nanotechnology are desirable.
  • Experience with production and analytical characterization of LNP formulation is a big plus.
  • Ability to write, edit, and follow standard operating procedures, make careful observations, maintain clear and complete records of lab work.‪

Strand does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from candidates.

title: Senior Systems Engineer (m/f/d) Reliability & Technical Solution
description:
About the Role

Autonomous ground vehicles rely on many interacting components to deliver dependable capabilities in the field. At ARX Robotics, we use Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) to manage this complexity from the first customer requirement to final verification. As a Senior Systems Engineer, you will define and maintain the MBSE framework that supports system-level design alongside safety, cybersecurity, and reliability engineering.

Your work ensures that nominal functions and critical safety, cybersecurity, and reliability artifacts fit together into a coherent system that performs as specified. You will also serve as the technical lead for resolving complex systems engineering challenges, directly shaping how our robotic platforms perform for the people who rely on them.

What You'll Build

  • Define and maintain the MBSE framework, including methods, guidelines, and templates that support system design, safety, cybersecurity, and reliability.
  • Write technical system specifications that translate customer, market, and mission needs into verifiable requirements.
  • Develop SysML models covering functional, behavioral, and architectural views as well as clear interface definitions.
  • Establish requirement structures, verification plans, and end-to-end traceability from initial need to final test.
  • Conduct architectural trade-off analyses to give engineering teams a clear, objective basis for design decisions.
  • Maintain alignment across requirements, models, design, and verification throughout the entire development lifecycle.
  • Manage system baselines and engineering changes so complex platforms remain controlled as they evolve.
  • Integrate certification, safety, and export control requirements into the system architecture from the start, while leading the technical resolution of systems engineering challenges.

What You Bring

  • A Master’s degree in Systems, Electrical, Mechanical, or Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • At least six years of professional experience applying systems engineering to complex technical systems. • Practical knowledge of the V-model and ASPICE, with a consistent focus on building quality into every development phase.
  • Hands-on MBSE experience using SysML, ideally within CATIA Magic or Cameo Systems Modeler.
  • Proven capability in requirements management using JAMA or comparable tools such as DOORS or Polarion.
  • Strong skills in analyzing requirements, deriving technical specifications, and designing verification strategies.
  • Clear written and spoken communication in both German and English to collaborate effectively across technical teams and external partners.
  • Experience in defense, aerospace, or automotive projects, particularly in safety-critical environments, is a plus.
  • Familiarity with industry standards such as ISO 15288, ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, or ISO 26262 is a plus.
  • Previous exposure to robotics, autonomous systems, embedded software, requirements-based testing, or system integration is a plus.

Please note: You do not need to meet every single requirement to apply. We welcome motivated candidates who are eager to grow into the role and develop their expertise further.

What We Offer

Join a mission-driven European defense tech company at a pivotal stage of growth, where you can help shape meaningful technology, take ownership early, and grow with the business!

  • Competitive compensation package including a bonus opportunity
  • 27 vacation days to start, increasing with tenure up to 30 days
  • Employer-supported pension contribution
  • Learning & development support and team events budget
  • Employee discounts and flexible benefits budget via Probonio
  • Hybrid working setup depending on role and team needs
  • Structured salary bands, levelling framework, and bi-annual development conversations
  • Referral bonus program, dog-friendly office, and relocation support where applicable

About Us

ARX is a dual-use technology company that specializes in developing autonomous unmanned systems and sensors for the European defence sector. Our dual-use unmanned ground systems and sensors assist NATO Armies and civilian first responders in tackling their most challenging problems by providing them with training and information to make better decisions and take effective actions in life-or-death situations.

As our team continues to expand rapidly, we are seeking motivated candidates who are excited to work in a highly energetic, creative, and innovative team dedicated to developing autonomous systems for challenging environments. We operate in a dynamic sector where collaboration, sharing innovative ideas, and developing novel problem-solving strategies are ingrained in our work culture.

If you are passionate about overcoming challenges that have a real impact on the security of our democracies, apply here to join ARX and help shape the future of dual-use technology!

ARX is an equal-opportunity employer, and we encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

title: Staff Software Engineer
description:
About IonQ:

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.

Location: This position can work onsite or hybrid from one of our offices or fully remote in the US.
Travel: Domestic, up to 10%
Job ID: 1959

The Role:

We are seeking a Staff Software Engineer to join our Resilience Engineering & Operations team. You will design and build software that helps operators run and maintain IonQ’s production quantum computers, so they can keep the fleet healthy, available, and performing reliably.

In this role, you will lead the design of operator tools and automation that deploy, configure, monitor, and validate a growing fleet of production systems. You will work side by side with operators, hardware engineers, and physicists to understand how production work actually gets done, then build software, documentation, and self-service capabilities that remove manual effort, reduce errors, and keep systems available. This is an opportunity to shape how IonQ runs its production fleet at a pivotal time as we scale.

Responsibilities:

  • Own the architecture and technical roadmap for operator tooling across production systems, including services, CLIs, APIs, and interfaces used to deploy, configure, and manage the fleet.
  • Design and build software that automates repetitive and error-prone production tasks, with safe defaults, clear feedback, and guardrails against misuse.
  • Treat operators as your customers: gather requirements, observe real workflows, and ship tools that measurably reduce effort and mistakes.
  • Enable operators to work independently by delivering self-service capabilities, clear documentation, runbooks, and hands-on training for the tools you build.
  • Build reliability into production software through sound design, thorough testing, fault tolerance, and instrumentation that makes system health visible to operators.
  • Develop automated validation, benchmarking, and performance verification that runs before changes reach production.
  • Lead complex, multi-quarter engineering initiatives from problem definition through delivery, including breaking down work for other engineers.
  • Set engineering standards for code quality, testing, security, and maintainability, including secure-by-default practices for CI/CD and secrets handling.
  • Mentor engineers through design reviews, code reviews, and pairing, and raise the technical bar across the organization.
  • Participates in an on-call rotation

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent industry experience in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • 6+ years of professional software engineering experience in a language like Python, Go, Rust, or C++.
  • A track record of designing and shipping production software that others use to run or manage systems, such as operational tooling, deployment automation, or fleet management software.
  • Strong software design skills, including API design, modular architecture, and testing strategy.
  • Solid understanding of Linux, networking, and distributed systems, and how software behaves when they fail in production.
  • Experience with containerization and orchestration (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) and Infrastructure as Code or configuration management (e.g., Terraform, Ansible).
  • The ability to explain technical concepts and tradeoffs clearly to engineers, operators, leadership, and stakeholders outside software.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • MS or PhD or equivalent industry experience in Computer Science, Aerospace, Mathematics, Physics, or a related field.
  • Experience building tools for hardware-coupled production environments (on-prem, lab, edge, or HPC) where individual machines differ in configuration.
  • Experience enabling non-software users through tool design, documentation, training, or usability research.
  • Experience integrating software with monitoring and logging tools (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, Mimir, Loki, ELK stack).
  • Depth in secure software development, such as software supply chain security, policy as code, and secure pipeline design.
  • Experience working with technical experts outside of traditional software engineering, such as electrical engineers, and physicists.
  • A background or emerging interest in quantum computing or physics.


The total compensation package includes base, bonus, equity, and a range of benefit options found on our career site.

If this role has a commission structure, the compensation range below just reflects the base compensation range.

$160,000—$200,000 USD
