title: Engineering - 12 Month Placement Scheme
description:
Career Area:

Students and Graduates

Job Description:

Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.

When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.

12 Month Industrial Placement Scheme

Discipline: Engineering

Location: Peterborough

Salary: £26,000, Share Scheme, Pension and 25 days annual leave (plus bank holidays), Employee Discount Scheme & Employee Assistance Program.

We currently have some exciting opportunities for industrial placement students to join Caterpillar across several of our sites. You will have the opportunity to work with others across our organisation and you will be directly involved, and at the heart of our business, participating on strategic projects.

*Please note that in order to be eligible to complete a 12-month Industrial Placement commencing July 2027, you must be in your penultimate year of study unless enrolled in an integrated master’s program.

What do we do?

Caterpillar Inc. is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines, and diesel-electric locomotives. Since 1925, we’ve been driving sustainable progress and helping customers build a better world through innovative products and services. Throughout the product life cycle, we offer services built on cutting-edge technology and decades of product expertise. These products and services, backed by our global dealer network, provide exceptional value to help our customers succeed.

We have a clear vision to be the global leader in providing customer value in the markets in which we operate. Our core values (Integrity, Excellence, Teamwork, Commitment and Sustainability) are key to our success.

At our Peterborough Campus we have a 500-person engineering team who design, develop, test and manufacture powertrain solutions for Caterpillar and third-party customers. Our world-class test facilities and partnerships with leading universities allow us to develop new technologies and support our global manufacturing sites. We have an ever-growing focus on next generation powertrain solutions, helping our customers progress towards Carbon Net Zero. We harness the power of data science and advanced simulation techniques, alongside traditional engineering disciplines, to create sustainable digital services and solutions that will power our customers’ future.

Diversity at Caterpillar

When we leverage our people's experiences, backgrounds, and cultures in an inclusive environment, we enable every individual to achieve their full potential, which drives business success. We are proud to be active partners with both the Society of Women Engineers (SWE) & Women's Engineering Society (WES). We also have numerous well supported employee resource groups. Caterpillar is an equal opportunity employer, and we welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds.

What experiences can we offer you?

As an equal opportunity employer, we value diversity at Caterpillar and believe the more experience you can gain early in your career the further you can go. That’s why during our yearlong scheme we place an emphasis on multiple diverse projects. You will have the opportunity to work and collaborate with people in Caterpillar facilities worldwide and we are looking for you to bring fresh, innovative ideas to solve complex technical problems. You will be a fully involved team member with responsibility and accountability for key project deliverables, with the support required to be successful.

Our placement roles have the additional benefit of a workplace mentor; this could be your manager or a technical expert who will support you throughout your time at Caterpillar and help you gain the professional development and skills you need to be set up for success! Our placement students can expect to return to university with further developed technical skills and experience of how University learning is applied to the workplace.

Job duties and responsibilities may include but are not limited to:

Our industrial placement training scheme consists of two six-month different engineering rotations. You will be a valued and active team member within busy development programs that influence Caterpillar’s Global products which in turn improve the lives of people around the world. Typically, individuals experience two of the following engineering team placements:

  • Simulation – systems, thermofluids and structural analysis
  • Designing, validation and testing components / engines / machines
  • Measurement and analysis of component / engine for noise, vibration, and structural integrity
  • Engine performance development – power and emissions development / analysis
  • Controls – machine integration, calibration, and algorithm development
  • Data analytics including commercial, machine learning and manufacturing
  • Power Systems Test Facility – emissions / measurement / systems analysis and improvements to support future development, process improvement and automation
  • Integrated powertrain and hybrid systems

This scheme aims to compliment your academic learning by experiencing how engineering principles are applied in varied real-world engine and powertrain development applications.

We offer you the opportunity to further grow your communication and teamwork skills, along with improving knowledge through daily collaboration with a variety of team members to deliver your team’s goals. Typically, this would include: Graduates, Technicians, Engineers, globally recognised Technical Specialists and people in Caterpillar facilities worldwide.

This scheme should help you to make informed future career decisions, through exposure to different roles and the subsequent multitude of collaboration teams and business partners. This experience will develop understanding of your own strengths and how they can positively contribute to a variety of roles, teams, and work styles. The knowledge gained should influence future decisions to help you flourish within a career in engineering beyond graduation.


Who are we looking for?

As the type of roles within our business are becoming more diverse, we are looking for people who are open minded, excellent problem solvers and who have an ability to learn quickly. You will be motivated, hard-working, and will embrace change. In return for your dedication and hard work, you will be provided with excellent career opportunities and strong support for your personal and career development to pursue a career within Caterpillar. Applicants will be on target to achieve a minimum of 2:2 honours degree level in a relevant discipline:

· Autosport or Motorsport Engineering

· Manufacturing Engineering

· Product Design Engineering

· Aeronautical Engineering

· Automotive Engineering

· Mechanical Engineering

· Aerospace Engineering

· Chemical Engineering

· General Engineering

· Mechatronics

· Physics

· Maths


There are big jobs to be done worldwide—building critical infrastructure, bolstering local economies, meeting the demand for energy—and that work is powered by our people. Our talented team creates sustainable, world-changing solutions that impact lives around the globe. Come join us!


Recruitment Process Guide

We're excited that you're considering a career with Caterpillar. Below is an overview of our Early Careers recruitment process and what you can expect at each stage.

  • Step 1: Online Application: To apply, simply complete our online application form and upload your CV before the advertised closing date.Our team will review all submissions & we'll keep you updated and let you know as soon as possible if you've been selected to progress to the next stage.
  • Step 2: Online Assessments & Video Interview: If you are selected to move forward in the process, you'll be invited to complete some online assessments, followed by a user-friendly video interview. Your responses will be reviewed by the hiring team and successful candidates will then be invited to attend an Assessment Centre which we anticipate will be held on the dates below onsite at our Peterborough facility so please try to keep that date free. We would also recommend that you check your spam emails and your Workday account for updates. At this stage, we envisage the assessment centres for this role will be held on these dates: 9th February 2027, 10th February 2027, 11th February 2027, 16th February 2027,17th February 2027
  • Step 3: In Person Assessment Centre: Our Assessment Centre is designed to help you showcase your potential through a range of interactive activities focused on competencies such as teamwork, communication, problem-solving, and decision-making.We aim to make the experience engaging, inclusive, and relaxed, giving you the best opportunity to demonstrate your strengths and learn more about Caterpillar.
  • Step 4: Offer: Following the Assessment Centre, the Caterpillar team will review all feedback and make hiring decisions. We aim to communicate outcomes and extend offers to successful candidates as quickly as possible. Placement students will start in late June 2027.

NOTES:

  • The panel cannot make assumptions when shortlisting therefore please demonstrate your qualifications and experience on your CV relevant to the criteria outlined.
  • Pending the number of applications, the criteria for the position may be enhanced to facilitate shortlisting. This may also include an adjustment to the application deadline date.
  • This position requires working onsite five days a week / all week.

This position requires working onsite five days a week.

Posting Dates:

November 16, 2026 - December 17, 2026

Caterpillar is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants of any age are encouraged to apply

Not ready to apply? Join our Talent Community.

Job Description

About The Role

The Global Trade Compliance Specialist supports the Center of Excellence (CoE) across tariff classification, origin, trade agreements and preferences, customs compliance, and emerging priorities. The role uses research, analytical thinking, technology, business-process knowledge, and strong attention to detail to convert regulatory requirements and business needs into practical, scalable, and audit-ready processes, tools, guidance, and controls, shifting across workstreams as priorities evolve.

Principal Accountabilities

1. Center of Excellence Operational Support & Governance

  • Maintain and improve CoE frameworks, standards, controls, and guidance across trade compliance disciplines.
  • Translate global requirements into consistent, practical tools, templates, and operating practices for regional and business teams.
  • Provide research, issue triage, and process support across classification, origin, trade agreements, preferences, data quality, and other priorities.

2. Classification, Origin, Trade Agreement & Preference Support

  • Support classification, origin, FTA, and preference determinations through product-data gathering, research, supplier certifications, and documentation.
  • Prepare and maintain working files, decision records, and audit-ready support packages.
  • Identify recurring issues, control gaps, and opportunities to improve related workflows.

3. Systems, Digitalization & Continuous Improvement

  • Support standardized workflows and system-enabled controls across CoE disciplines.
  • Assist with testing, documentation, enhancements, and user support for trade systems, data models, automation, and reporting.
  • Advance improvements that reduce manual effort, increase visibility, strengthen audit readiness, and enable scalable execution.

4. Regulatory Intelligence, Audit & CoE Communication

  • Monitor relevant regulatory developments and summarize their business impact.
  • Turn technical requirements into clear guidance, communications, training, and leadership summaries.
  • Support internal audits and risk assessments across the CoE’s scope.

Knowledge and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience in business, supply chain, finance, data analytics, information systems, legal studies, engineering, communications, or a related field.
  • Strong analytical, research, written communication, documentation, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Ability and willingness to quickly learn trade compliance concepts, regulatory frameworks, internal systems, and technical product information.
  • Ability to learn regulatory and technical subject matter and convert it into practical, repeatable, and auditable processes.
  • Strong judgment when using AI, research tools, and other information sources, including the ability to validate outputs and recognize incomplete or unreliable information.
  • Comfort working with structured and unstructured data, business systems, product information, and detailed documentation.
  • Fluent in English.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience in business, supply chain, finance, data analytics, information systems, legal studies, engineering, communications, or a related field.

title: Solution Architect
description:
Founded in Switzerland in 1968, Zühlke is owned by its partners and located across Europe and Asia. We are a global transformation partner, with engineering and innovation in our DNA. We're trusted to help clients envision and build their businesses for the future – to run smarter today while adapting for tomorrow’s markets, customers, and communities. Our multidisciplinary teams specialise in tech strategy and business innovation, digital solutions and applications, and device and systems engineering. We excel in complex, regulated spaces including health and finance, connecting strategy, tech implementation, and operational services to help clients become more effective, resilient businesses.

If you share our values and want to do the best work, for the right reasons, we can offer you the chance to do it on a global scale and play a real role in shaping our exciting journey.

The role.

We are looking for an experienced and passionate Solution Architect to join our Hong Kong team. At Zühlke, you will work closely with engineering teams and clients to design and deliver scalable, reliable, and sustainable technology solutions. In this role, you will take architectural ownership of key capabilities within an existing business-critical platform. You will focus on understanding the current system, its capabilities and limitations, and designing solutions that extend, integrate, or modernise existing components while ensuring operational continuity. Working alongside other Solution Architects and technical leads, you will guide three engineering squads, translating high-level architectural decisions into practical implementation approaches. You will contribute to solution design, technical discovery, and continuous improvement while ensuring alignment across the wider platform. The technology environment includes Java, Kotlin, React Native, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, and AWS. The role is based in Hong Kong, with occasional visits to local client branches and no overseas travel required.



What's important to us.

  • You have proven experience in solution architecture, with the ability to understand complex existing systems, analyse their components and dependencies, and design practical, scalable solutions.
  • You have strong structural thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate architectural options, identify trade-offs, and make sound technical decisions.
  • You have experience integrating, extending, or modernising existing systems while maintaining stability and operational continuity.
  • You have solid knowledge of distributed systems, API design, event-driven architecture, integration patterns, data consistency, and failure handling.
  • You are proficient in architecture documentation and modelling techniques, including C4 models, sequence diagrams, interface specifications, and Architecture Decision Records (ADRs).
  • You have experience gathering and analysing technical requirements, facilitating solution design workshops, and translating business needs into practical architecture.
  • You can define and evaluate non-functional requirements, including performance, security, availability, maintainability, and cost.
  • You understand modern software engineering practices, including CI/CD, automated testing, cloud platforms, observability, and technical debt management.
  • You are comfortable collaborating with multiple engineering squads, guiding technical leads, and influencing architectural decisions without direct authority.
  • You have excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to engage effectively with technical teams and business stakeholders.
  • You have strong English communication skills. Conversational Cantonese is a significant advantage, particularly for interactions with client teams during local branch visits.

It would be an advantage if you also have:

  • A hands-on software engineering background, with experience developing and maintaining production systems.
  • Familiarity with Java, Kotlin, React Native, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, or AWS.
  • Experience with data and media streaming, retail terminals, or in-store devices.
  • Knowledge of data migration approaches, including schema evolution, reconciliation, and cutover planning.
  • Experience working in consulting or multi-vendor environments, with exposure to technical leadership or mentoring.

What we offer

  • Work life blend: We offer a safe & healthy workplace, with flexible working hours and the possibility to work from home.
  • Profit share scheme: In addition to your annual salary, you may receive a profit share defined by the company's success in the previous year.
  • Global and Diverse Zühlke community: Witness how colleagues from all our offices across the globe come together to create a unique, positive and inclusive work culture, learning from one another at annual team camps, and celebrating year-end parties and other local festivities.
  • Committed to development: We are committed to the growth of our people and are investing in your development. We're empowering you to build the skills you need to make a positive impact, both personally and for our clients, today and in the future.

If you feel you don't meet all the requirements, we are still happy to get to know you, learn more about your ambitions and ideas and look forward to receiving your application!


We welcome people from all backgrounds, regardless of their gender, personality, national origin, race, religion, colour, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, disability or veteran status.

title: Senior Security Engineer (DevSecOps)
description:
About AI71

AI71 is an industry leader in artificial intelligence, delivering innovative solutions that empower developers, businesses and governments to solve complex challenges. AI71 builds secure, enterprise-ready applications powered by cutting-edge technology—tailored for knowledge workers and sector-specific needs. AI71 bridges the gap between advanced AI and real-world impact. Guided by a strong commitment to research and responsibility, we create transformative solutions that drive progress and empower communities.

The Role

As a Senior Security Engineer on the DevSecOps team, you will work alongside developers to secure AI products running on Kubernetes for enterprise clients in the UAE. You will own product security end to end, build controls, ship fixes, and partner with our managed Security Operations Center (SOC) on incident response. Our products ship as managed SaaS and as on-premises installs, including fully disconnected, air-gapped environments, so your work protects some of the most sensitive deployments in the region.

What You'll Do

  • Own security for our products end to end, including threat models and design reviews.
  • Design and implement secure networking and zero-trust access: segmentation, ingress and egress control, and a web application firewall (WAF).
  • Run and extend CI security pipelines: static application security testing (SAST), secret scanning, software composition analysis (SCA) with software bills of materials (SBOM), and container scanning, including offline scanning and patching for air-gapped installs.
  • Triage vulnerabilities by whether they are reachable and exploitable, not just by CVSS score, and drive fixes with developers.
  • Automate patching across environments.
  • Harden Kubernetes and cloud environments: pod security, network policies, identity and access management (IAM) with least privilege, and secrets managers.
  • Coordinate with pentest vendors and support compliance (UAE IA, OWASP ASVS) through remediation and evidence gathering.
  • Handle incident response together with our managed SOC.

What You'll Bring

• Experience: Bring 5–8 years in security engineering or DevSecOps, or in DevOps/site reliability engineering (SRE) with a strong security focus.
• Cloud and containers: Demonstrate hands-on experience with Kubernetes and a major cloud provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
• Networking: Apply strong fundamentals in TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, firewalls, and segmentation.
• CI/CD: Show experience building and running pipelines in GitLab CI or a similar tool.
• Application security: Apply working knowledge of the OWASP Top 10.
• Coding: Script in Python or Bash, and read and write code confidently rather than only running tools.

Great Pluses / Preferred Experience

• Experience with Terraform, Helm, Cloudflare, Teleport, or Argo CD.
• On-premises infrastructure experience, including air-gapped environments.
• Threat modeling or hands-on pentesting experience; OSCP or CKS certification is a plus.
• AI and large language model (LLM) security experience: prompt injection, agent permissions, and sandbox isolation.
• Arabic language skills.

Why AI71

• Mission-Driven Work: Work on cutting-edge AI applications with a talented and passionate team, solving real-world challenges in critical sectors.
• Unparalleled Opportunity: This is a chance to innovate and solve real-world challenges using AI at a company with unique access to world-leading models and resources.
• Career Growth: We offer competitive compensation, benefits, and significant career growth opportunities as a foundational member of the team.
• World-Class Environment: Enjoy a flexible working environment and the latest tools & technologies needed to do your best work.

As Mechanical Specialist in the days team at Skelmersdale, you’ll lead defined maintenance activities with a focus on mechanical systems. title: Senior Program Officer, K-12 Scaling Measurement, Learning and Evaluation
description:
The Foundation

We are the largest nonprofit fighting poverty, disease, and inequity around the world. Founded on a simple premise: people everywhere, regardless of identity or circumstances, should have the chance to live healthy, productive lives. We believe our employees should reflect the rich diversity of the global populations we aim to serve. We provide an exceptional benefits package to employees and their families which include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with no premiums, generous paid time off, paid family leave, foundation-paid retirement contribution, regional holidays, and opportunities to engage in several employee communities. As a workplace, we’re committed to creating an environment for you to thrive both personally and professionally.

The Team

The K-12 Teaching and Learning team works to develop the products and approaches that can support teachers to ensure that no K-12 student remains below grade level for longer than 3 years. To do that, we invest in the development, validation, and adoption of effective K-12 curriculum and AI-enabled tutoring solutions, with a focus on math across early learning, middle grades, and high school. We also support the market and system conditions necessary to support the safe and effective scaling of AI-enabled tools that support the growth of students below grade level. Our strategy is organized across four sub-teams — R&D, Enactment, Solutions, and Engagement — working together to build rigorous evidence, scale what works, and shape the conditions that allow proven solutions to reach every learner. Embedded within and across these sub-teams, our Measurement, Learning, and Evaluation (MLE) function ensures that our investments are grounded in strong evidence-based hypotheses, that we collect relevant and timely evidence to test those hypotheses, and that we use that evidence to continuously improve those hypotheses over time. We are committed to advancing educational equity through the application of Targeted Universalism principles, and to building an inclusive, collaborative team culture.

Your Role
You are responsible for developing and managing a portfolio of MLE investments focused on the K-12 strategy's theory of scale for AI-enabled curriculum and teacher support products that support the growth of students below grade level — measuring scale readiness, market dynamics, and the attitudes and behaviors of key actors at scale. You ensure the outputs of those investments are timely, useful, and used to support continuous improvement and decision-making. You serve as an embedded MLE partner to both the Engagement and Solutions sub-teams, bridging their approaches to scale and connecting the K-12 strategy to division-level Enablers work. You have expertise in scale measurement methodology, market surveillance, and demand-side research in education. You bring significant experience in the application of that knowledge to support organizational improvement and decision-making.


*Our preference is for this role to be located in Seattle, WA. In some cases we may be open to considering Washington, DC as the work location. Relocation assistance is available for the hired candidate if they do not live within a commutable distance to one of those office locations. No Visa support is available for this position.


*Applications accepted until 5 PM Pacific Time on Monday, December 7th, 2026.

What You'll Do

Identify and fill key portfolio hypothesis evidence needs (40%)

  • Serve as an embedded MLE partner to key scale-focused bodies of work on the Engagement sub-team and Solutions sub-team, enabling deep familiarization with the strategic hypotheses, grants, and grantees within and across those bodies of work
  • Design and manage a portfolio of grants and contracts to monitor, test, and improve those body of work hypotheses (e.g., survey, market monitoring, attitudes research, projection modeling)
  • Support quality of MLE in programmatic investments through scaled capacity-building approaches and, as needed, more intensive support on individual investments
  • Attend to the equity and targeted universalism implications of grant and contract portfolio to improve the quality of MLE practice to support equitable outcomes for targeted populations
  • Ensure that outputs and learnings from those investments are relevant, timely, and useful to strategy and partner decision-making

Support use of evidence for decision-making (40%)

  • Work closely with body of work Deputy Directors and Strategy Officers to ensure that progress and tests of strategy hypotheses are well-communicated and understood by strategy, division, and foundation leadership
  • Support reporting processes, knowledge management systems, capacity-building supports, and learning routines that ensure staff and partners have timely and useful access and sense-making support to apply evidence to improve hypotheses and decision-making

Improve and implement strategy-wide approaches to MLE (20%)

  • Connect needs and experiences of portfolio hypothesis testing and improvement to the improvement and implementation of strategy-wide MLE approaches
  • Connect to larger field trends and innovations in MLE and bring back that knowledge to inform and improve strategy-wide approaches
  • Build reputation and awareness of K-12 approaches to MLE by engaging with external experts, conferences, convenings, and other speaking and networking opportunities


Your Experience

  • Through a relevant advanced degree or significant prior professional experience, proven expertise in measurement and evaluation methodology, including theories of influence or scale, survey and behavioral research at scale, market monitoring, and demand-side measurement
  • Through a relevant credential or significant prior professional experience, proven ability to credibly communicate complex data and evidence for multiple audiences and support its application to decision-making
  • Significant experience working across multiple teams or portfolios simultaneously, with demonstrated ability to coordinate priorities, maintain coherence, and build trust across diverse stakeholders
  • Significant experience building and managing external partnerships with researchers, evaluators, and market research firms
  • A commitment to meeting the needs of all K-12 students, regardless of background and circumstances, and the ability to apply that commitment to day-to-day work

*Must have unrestricted work authorization in the country where this position is located. The Foundation does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. This includes direct company sponsorship and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (eg: H-1B, O-1, L-1, E, OPT, STEM-OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.).


The salary range for this role is $173,000 to $259,600 USD. We recognize high-wage market differences in Seattle, WA and Washington D.C., where our offices are located. The range for this role in these locations is $190,300 to $285,500 USD. As a mission-driven organization, we strive to balance competitive pay with our mission. New hires salaries are typically between the range minimum and the salary range midpoint. Actual placement in the range will depend on a candidate's job-related skills, experience, and expertise, as evaluated during the interview process.
